newsitem.title: PERU: Bear Stearns sees Peru's '97 growth lower on siege.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns sees Peru's '97 growth lower on siege.

text.p: New York-based Bear Stearns & Co said Monday the Peruvian economy would experience lower-than-expected growth next year due to the current hostage crisis in Lima.
"Peru had started a mild recovery at the time of the attack. We think this will be put on hold," Bear Stearns analyst David Malpass said in a report.
Malpass did not say by how much Bear Stearns would lower its estimate of 1997 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth from its original forecast of 4.0 to 5.5 percent.
The government's official projection for 1997 economic growth is 5.0 percent.

Bear Stearns said the attack by leftist rebels on the Japanese ambassador's residence would likely reduce investment from Japan, have a "less notable" negative impact on other investments and touristm, and "tarnish" the image of Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori.

"This is particularly harmful to Peru since Japan has been a strong supporter of Fujimori. The actual enthusiasm will be sharply diminshed, no matter what Japan's public stance is once the situation is resolved," the report said.

Despite Peruvians "pro-Peru" reaction to the siege, "Fujimori's image of being lucky -- a huge positive for him -- has been tarnished. The extent depends on the outcome of the hostage situation," Malpass wrote.
